content: 1. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the absorption of gemifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are administered orally. To minimize this effect, separate the administration of these agents by at least 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 2. Magnesium oxide also decreases the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Administer the agents at least 2 hours apart and monitor the patient closely. 3. Magnesium sulfate reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 4. Magnesium supplements can decrease the effectiveness of gemifloxacin by forming an insoluble complex in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing drug absorption. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 3 hours after gemifloxacin. Monitor the patient closely. 5. Gemifloxacin and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 6. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and meclofenamate increases the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy as needed and monitor closely. 7. Gemifloxacin and mefenamic acid also increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 8. Both gemifloxacin and mefloquine prolong the QTc interval, which may increase the risk of arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 9. Gemifloxacin and meloxicam increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures when used together. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Gemifloxacin may reduce the effectiveness of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of mestranol. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 12. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and methadone significantly prolongs the QTc interval, increasing the risk of serious arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Gemifloxacin and methyl aminolevulinate increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, including enhanced photosensitizing effects. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and methylprednisolone increases the risk of tendon rupture due to the combined effects of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Gemifloxacin reduces the effectiveness of oral microbiota products by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. Avoid concurrent use. 16. Gemifloxacin increases midazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 17. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and midostaurin prolongs the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Gemifloxacin and mifepristone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 19. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of miglitol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 20. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and mirtazapine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Gemifloxacin and mometasone inhaled increase the risk of tendon rupture when used together. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and nabumetone increases the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Gemifloxacin and naproxen also increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 24. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of nateglinide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 25. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and nilotinib significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Gemifloxacin and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and octreotide prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Gemifloxacin and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Limited data suggest that olanzapine may rarely cause significant QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and olodaterol inhaled prolongs the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Gemifloxacin and ondansetron significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or other risk factors. 31. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and osilodrostat prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Gemifloxacin and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring in patients taking QTc-prolonging drugs. 33. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of gemifloxacin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and oxaliplatin significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Gemifloxacin and oxaprozin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Gemifloxacin increases oxazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 37. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and ozanimod prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients taking QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 38. Gemifloxacin and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and panobinostat significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Gemifloxacin reduces the effectiveness of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 41. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and pasireotide prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Gemifloxacin and pazopanib significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and pentamidine significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 44. Gemifloxacin and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Gemifloxacin decreases the effects of phenytoin through an unknown mechanism. There are also reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and pimavanserin significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Gemifloxacin and pimozide significantly prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of pioglitazone through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 49. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and piroxicam increases the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Gemifloxacin and pitolisant significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 51. Polysaccharide iron reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 52. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and ponesimod significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 53. Gemifloxacin and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and prednisolone increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Gemifloxacin and prednisone also increase the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and primaquine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Probenecid increases gemifloxacin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 58. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and procainamide significantly prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 59. Gemifloxacin and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and promethazine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Gemifloxacin and propafenone significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 62. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and protriptyline prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Gemifloxacin reduces the effectiveness of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. 64. Gemifloxacin increases quazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 65. Quercetin reduces the effects of gemifloxacin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 66. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and quetiapine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT intervals. 67. Gemifloxacin and quinidine significantly prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 68. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and quinine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Gemifloxacin and quizartinib both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Conduct frequent ECG monitoring if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 70. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and ranolazine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of repaglinide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 72. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 73. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and rilpivirine prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid combining rilpivirine with drugs that increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 74. Gemifloxacin and risperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and romidepsin prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Rose hips reduce gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 77. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of rosiglitazone through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 78. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and salmeterol prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of saxagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 80. Selinexor increases the risk of neurological toxicities when combined with gemifloxacin. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid selinexor with other medications that cause dizziness or confusion. 81. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and selpercatinib prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Gemifloxacin and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and sevoflurane prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 84. Gemifloxacin and siponimod significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 85. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and sitagliptin enhances pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution, as quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 86. Sodium bicarbonate reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by 2 hours. 87. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and sodium citrate/citric acid reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
